key_insight: Airfoil2Vec uses spectral geometry encoding to make neural surrogates predict airfoil flow fields much faster while staying accurate across new shapes and angles of attack.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid aerodynamic screening for motorsport and automotive downforce design, reducing reliance on expensive CFD runs.
method: ~10,000 steady 2D RANS simulations of NACA 4-digit downforce airfoils form the dataset.
Airfoil2Vec combines the joint contour spectrum with separate spectral encodings of camber and thickness.
Models are tested against neural fields, neural ODEs, MLPs, graph models, and other spectral conditioning methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong generalization on angle-of-attack interpolation, unseen NACA geometries, and unseen non-NACA airfoils, with orders-of-magnitude speedups over CFD.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the learned geometry encoding transfers to airfoils outside the training distribution or to conditions beyond steady, incompressible 2D RANS.
paper_title: Airfoil2Vec: Spectral Geometry-Conditioned Neural Surrogate Models for Airfoil Aerodynamics and a Downforce-Generating CFD Dataset
